sentences.text: Sichuanosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform that lived in China during the Late Jurassic and possibly the Early Cretaceous.
This animal was small, with a skull measuring about 6.1 centimeters in the type species and approximately 6.7 centimeters in S. shuhanensis.
The type species S. huidongensis was described in 1995 by Peng Guangzhao based on a nearly complete skeleton found in Jurassic sediments of the Shangshaximiao Formation in the Sichuan Basin.
The species S. shuhanensis is later, with its fossils likely dating to the Early Cretaceous.
Sichuanosuchus moved on four legs, possessing relatively long and slender forelimbs.
It had heterodont dentition with large, serrated, laterally flattened front teeth shaped like canines and lower posterior teeth, indicating it ate meat.
Sichuanosuchus likely led a semi-aquatic life.
Dollman et al. (2018) erected the clade Shartegosuchoidea to include Shartegosuchidae, Sichuanosuchus, Zosuchus, and Shantungosuchus.
Fossil evidence places Sichuanosuchus in the Bathonian to Callovian stages, between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.
